summary.headline: Radiant CMS standalone revenue flat in FY26 at INR1.69 trillion cash handled; consolidated PAT fell to INR280 million from INR470 million on fintech losses.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue was flat YoY in FY26, with cash handled up about 1% to INR1.69 trillion, as railways region losses and an e-commerce client loss offset growth. Standalone Q4 EBITDA margin was 15%, up from 13.6% (some sources cite 30.6% for Q3, which conflicts with the 13.6% cited by the CFO). Consolidated PAT dropped to INR280 million from INR470 million, mainly from losses at fintech subsidiary Radiant Acemoney after the PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025. Management set targets of breakeven for RVL and Acemoney in H1 FY27 and consolidated EBITDA of 15%+, while the buyback was described as under consideration.

segments.name: Core retail cash management (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat in FY26 after losing railways regions (about INR9-10 crore annualised) and an e-commerce logistics client (about INR4 crore annualised). Service points reached 77,521, with 2,173 added in Q4 and 118 new clients and 230 new customers added during the year. E-commerce grew 21%; petroleum and organised retail also grew well.

segments.name: Radiant Valuable Logistics (RVL)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR60.7 million in FY26 with a loss of about INR60 million. Management expects breakeven in H1 FY27 and says 25-30% of lanes have turned profitable; it added five marquee jewellery chains and targets 20% steady-state EBITDA margin rising to 30%.

segments.name: Radiant Acemoney (fintech subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR287.8 million in FY26 (+19.6%), with about 1.5 lakh POS merchants onboarded and about 60,000 soundboxes added. Q4 was weak after the PIDF subsidy ended on 31 December 2025; Q4 standalone subsidiary revenue was a little under INR1 crore. Over 10,000 business correspondents are now live, and management targets H1 FY27 breakeven.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for consolidated revenue of INR5 billion and PAT margin of 11-12% in FY27, with mid-teens longer-term PAT growth; no formal guidance was issued.
Core business revenue growth target of 12-14% (mid-teens per Q&A) in FY27 is needed for PAT of about INR60 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA immediate target of about 15%+ and breakeven for both RVL and Acemoney in H1 FY27.
Acemoney breakeven needs roughly INR4.5 crore quarterly revenue, per the Q&A discussion of the analyst's estimate.
Management expects positive impact from bank discussions on fuel-cost pass-through (cash logistics association approached banks) from H1 FY27; no outcome yet.
Direct customers are about 18% of revenue, with a target of around 30% within two years.
capex_capacity: Service points 77,521 at year end; 2,173 added in Q4 FY26 but total points slightly down YoY due to railways losses. Management says the point-addition plan is unchanged.
Dedicated cash van contract rolling out; two to three more large contracts in pipeline. Cash-on-operations is about 12% of revenue.
Acemoney has 1.5 lakh+ POS machines and about 60,000 soundboxes, with plans for more deployments via small finance banks and NBFCs.
Radiant is applying for a payment aggregator licence at the holding-company level with the RBI.
demand_pricing: Railways and e-commerce losses weighed on core revenue; management is pursuing direct clients, dedicated cash vans, and smaller and cooperative/rural banks.
A large project order from an existing customer began rollout from 1 April 2026; an analyst estimated it adds 3-4% to the top line.
Cash logistics association has approached banks on fuel-cost charges; management expects a favourable outcome to be possible from H1 FY27.

Acemoney sells through tripartite arrangements with small finance banks and payment aggregators, with one-time rollout fees plus transaction revenue. Management says transaction revenue carries no material cost.
Management said that 37 banks offer retail cash management services but only two nationwide providers exist, which it cited as a competitive advantage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the direct-customer share of revenue and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct customers are about 18% of revenue, up from about 1% earlier and about 13% last quarter; management says 30% is a reasonable target within two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a buyback given its cash and valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is being explored with larger shareholders and advisers, with no decision yet; it also highlighted its dividend record.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FY26 losses at RVL and Acemoney?
qa_highlights.answer: RVL lost about INR60 million and Acemoney about INR100 million at PAT level in FY26; both are targeted to turn PAT-positive, ideally in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-time exceptional item impact on the subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO put the exceptional item impact on the subsidiary at about INR31 million; management said the full amount of a fraud loss in Assam has been provided in the books, with recovery uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Acemoney growth sustainable now that the PIDF subsidy has ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is no longer dependent on PIDF, and that POS and soundboxes remain remunerative via transaction revenue, with growth from small finance bank and NBFC roll-outs.

qa_highlights.question: How will RVL reach breakeven given lane-based cost structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had opened too many lanes without sales; it now focuses on a set of lanes where fixed costs are covered by added volume, with 25-30% of lanes already profitable.

risks_watch: Acemoney breakeven in H1 FY27 depends on new bank and NBFC roll-outs; quarterly transaction revenue is currently only about INR70 lakh.
Core revenue growth remains unproven after flat FY26; railways and e-commerce losses weigh on the base.
Fuel and wage inflation pressure on standalone margins; outcome of bank talks on fuel charges is open.
Recovery from the Assam fraud is uncertain; the full amount has been provided, so any recovery would be upside.
Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 10.7% (or 8.5%, as cited on the call); watch for the 15%+ target.
Management's inconsistent figures on Q3 standalone EBITDA margin (30.6% vs 13.6%) need reconciliation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on turnaround timelines (breakeven H1 FY27 for both subsidiaries), but cautious on core growth: FY26 was described as subdued, and several answers were imprecise or deferred (fraud recovery, buyback, fuel-charge outcome).
